subject: Re: Data residency & export controls — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health - Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency & export controls — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Liam / Acme security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the outstanding security/compliance items for the evaluation: 

Summary (call highlights)
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II engagement in progress; interim summary attached. Full Type II report expected Q3 2026.
- EU region & residency: We offer a dedicated EU region (data at rest stored in Dublin) for customer workloads; see attached residency matrix for specifics.
- Cross-border transfers: For backups/operations we rely on contractual safeguards (standard contractual clauses) and our EU-only processing option.
- Key management: Customers can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations; we also offer Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys.
- Export controls / OFAC / ITAR: We don't intentionally process ITAR-controlled technical data by default; we can discuss constrained controls if required. 

Open action items / next steps
1) Acme to send completed vendor security questionnaire — we'll use that as the canonical list for gaps (Liam suggested this on the call).
2) Redwood to provide a SOC2 summary + pointer to cert artifacts (attached and link below).
3) Redwood to clarify KMS/BYOK flows and whether any US-based admin access is required for EU-resident workloads.
4) Align on procurement requirements for export-control screening (if ITAR/OFAC filters needed).

Attachments: eu-data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

I'll coordinate internally on the questionnaire responses once you share it. If you can drop the completed questionnaire by Tuesday EOD (your timezone), we'll aim to return completed answers within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. Attached is Acme's vendor security questionnaire (we highlighted a few priority sections). A couple of quick clarifications we need answered in your responses: 

- Encryption & key management: Please confirm whether Redwood-managed keys ever result in plaintext key material being exported outside EU, or whether customer BYOK keys are stored/managed solely in-region for EU deployments.
- Cross-border access: If we deploy in the EU region, can Redwood US-based support or SRE teams access unredacted customer data for troubleshooting? If so, what controls / JIT processes are in place?
- Export controls: We have a procurement flag for ITAR/OFAC — please confirm if Redwood has any OFAC screening process for stored data or for exports.

We aim to get this questionnaire back by COB Monday (UK timezone). Appreciate the SOC2 artifact link and the residency matrix.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Engineering | Acme Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data residency & export controls — vendor questionnaire (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa — I'll take lead on compliance language and start pulling the SOC2 artifacts. Quick notes / initial answers below: 

- SOC 2: We have a SOC2 Type II engagement in progress; interim summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). The Type II report is scheduled to be finalized in Aug 2026. SOC2 artifacts (control mapping, auditor letter) available at: https://drive.redwood.com/AcmeHealth/SOC2-TypeII-2026

- KMS / BYOK: Priyom and Michael — please confirm, but current platform behavior for EU-dedicated deployments is that customer BYOK key material is provisioned and stored in-region when using a customer-managed KMS integration. For Redwood-managed keys, keys are HSM-backed and we can restrict key storage to EU region on dedicated deployments. We do not export plaintext key material as part of normal operations.

- Cross-border access: Support/SRE have role-based access and break-glass processes. Where EU residency is required, access is limited and audited; we can provide a summary of JIT access controls and an admin access matrix. Michael, please add specifics on logging/audit retention.

- Export controls / OFAC / ITAR: Initial position — Redwood does not perform OFAC screening on arbitrary stored customer content. For export-control concerns (ITAR), we treat requests as a special procurement/legal review: if Acme has ITAR-controlled data, we will need to engage legal to confirm whether additional controls or contract language are required. Rachel (compliance) to coordinate with Legal if the customer flags ITAR.

I'll assemble proposed answers for the questionnaire by Wed EOD PST so Marissa can send consolidated responses to Acme on Thu. Priyom, Michael — can you confirm the technical bits by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Manager, Compliance & Trust | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
